what: 2-D body-fitted RANS of the KVLCC2 rudder section (NACA-0018 idealisation, chord 0.17057 m) at model-scale Reynolds number

audit.verdict: FAILED / WITHHELD — the polar is not physically admissible and is not used for any verdict

symmetry_check.comment: the zero-incidence lift vanishes to 1e-3 of the drag scale, so the discrete symmetry of the solver holds

audit.lift_sign: cl becomes *negative* as the incidence rises (+10 deg -> cl = -0.141), which cannot be a physical rudder polar
audit.drag_level: cd = 0.58-0.67, two orders of magnitude above a 0.18-thickness section at Re = 1.8e5 (expected cd ~ 0.01-0.03): the force is dominated by an unresolved boundary layer / numerical diffusion

mesh_convergence.comment: cd changes by 35 % between coarse and medium and cl by 20 %; a three-level GCI was attempted but the fine run did not finish inside the 70 min budget, so criterion (f) on the CFD mesh is NOT met

audit.root_cause: the C-grid resolves neither the wall-normal boundary layer nor the wake at this cell count; with Spalart-Allmaras at y+ >> 1 the eddy viscosity destroys the pressure distribution. The repository's verified NACA cases used 2000+ iterations on a hybrid gmsh mesh, not a structured 96x32 C-grid
audit.consequence: the analytic finite-aspect polar is used for the manoeuvring chain; the CFD rudder face is recorded as an honest failure with the numbers needed to reproduce it
